summary: Ram Chandra Kak was a scholar of Indology and archaeology. He studied at Sri Pratap College (~1909–1913) and under John Marshall (1914–1919), later serving as curator at Sri Pratap Singh Museum (~1914–1919) and Director of Archæology and Research in Jammu and Kashmir (1919–1929).

Ram Chandra Pandeya worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, studying under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale and T. R. V. Murti. At the University of Delhi, he was Professor and Head of Buddhist Studies (~1966–1973) and an acharya (~1973–1996).

Indologist and linguist Ram Karan Sharma studied at Patna University and the University of California, Berkeley under Murray Barnson Emeneau (PhD ~1957–1959). He served as vice chancellor at Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1974–1980) and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1984–1985).

Ram Mohan Roy was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He founded Atmiya Sabha (1814), Presidency University (1816), Anglo-Hindu School (1822), Mirat-ul-Akhbar (1822), Vedanta College (1826), the Calcutta Unitarian Committee, and Brahmo Samaj (1828).

Ram Niwas Pandey works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute of Archaeology, and under doctoral supervisor Hit Narayan Jha.

Ram Prasad Bhatt works in Indology and linguistics. He completed his doctoral studies at Hemwati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University (2003–2006) and held posts at the University of Leipzig (2002–2003) and the University of Hamburg (2003).

Ram Shankar Bhattacharya was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Raghunatha Shastri. He held appointments at Tikmani Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya as a teacher, and at the All-India Kashiraj Trust and Banaras Hindu University as a research assistant.

Ram Shankar Tripathi specialized in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He served as Head of Buddhist Philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1977, 1989–1998) and Dean of the Faculty of Śabdavidyā at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2001).

Historian and Indologist Ram Sharan Sharma studied at Patna University and SOAS (PhD ~1954–1956) under A. L. Basham and Wilhelm Rau. He headed the history departments at Patna University (1958–1973) and Delhi University (1973–1978), and founded the ICHR (1972).
Rama Kant Agnihotri is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He earned a doctorate from York University (1973–1975) and served on the editorial board at the University of Delhi (1980–2010).

Rama Mishra Shastri was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University as Professor (attested 1882–1889) and as assistant Professor of Sāṅkhya (attested 1914).

Rama Nath Sharma studied at Banaras Hindu, Allahabad, Agra, and Rochester (PhD ~1966–1971), and under Raghunatha Sharma and Ramaprasada Tripathi. A linguist and Indologist, he taught at Allahabad (1962–1966) and Rochester (1971–1976) before becoming Professor at Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1976).

Indologist and linguist Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar studied under Martin Haug and earned degrees from Mumbai and Göttingen (PhD 1885). He was a professor at Elphinstone College (~1868–1882) and Deccan College (~1882–1893), and served as Vice Chancellor of Mumbai University (~1893–1894).

Indologist Ramanath Pandey earned degrees from AMU, Delhi University, and Ranchi University (PhD 1984–1989). He held positions at Delhi University (1995–2001) and Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (2004–2022), and became a Professor at Parshwanath Vidyapeeth in 2025.

Ramanatha Dikshita was an Indology scholar who worked in the Sadholal Research Department at Sarasvati Bhavana (attested 1944) and served as Head of the Veda Department at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi (attested 1970).

Ramaprasad Chanda studied at Scottish Church College and worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He lectured at the University of Calcutta (1920–1921), served as Superintendent of Archaeology at the Indian Museum, Kolkata (1921–1932), and presided over the Indian Anthropological Institute (1938–1942).
Ramaprasada Tripathi was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who served as a former vice-chancellor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1976; also attested there in 2001).

Indologist Ramaranjan Mukherji earned degrees from Calcutta University (PhD ~1946–1953) and Jadavpur University (DLitt 1964). He headed Sanskrit at Jadavpur (1956), served as vice chancellor of Burdwan (1970–1984) and Rabindra Bharati (-1987), and was chancellor of National Sanskrit University.

Ramashastri Bhagavatacharya was an Indology scholar who held posts as an assistant professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1891) and as a teacher/professor at Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi (attested 1891).

Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Vidyapith, L. D. Arts College (attested 1938), and S. L. U. Arts and H. & P. Thakore Commerce College for Women (attested 1938).
